title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-ava-martinez
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for the SSE / chunking / backpressure flakiness we've been hitting in hosted-api (esp when client is slow or through proxies). Trying to capture repro commands, logs seen, hypotheses and quick hacks tried.

Observed symptoms:
- Client sometimes receives huge initial payload then nothing until connection closes (perceived stall). Other times receives garbled partial JSON objects (stream framing lost).
- Happens more often behind Nginx/ALB and when payloads are chunked by runtime (Transfer-Encoding: chunked).
- Errors seen in logs:
  - server: "write EPIPE" (when client disconnects)
  - nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"
  - client: JSON parse error on partial chunk (unexpected end)

Quick repro (minimal):
1) Start local dev server that streams server-sent events (express example):
   node server.js (basic SSE handler that writes JSON lines with res.write)

2) Curl client that simulates slow consumption:
   curl --no-buffer http://localhost:3000/sse -N | pv -qL 10 > /dev/null
   (pv -L 10 throttles read to 10 bytes/sec)

3) Variant through nginx reverse proxy config (proxy_buffering on/off) to reproduce proxy buffering behaviors.

Commands I used to capture behavior:
- curl --no-buffer -v http://localhost:3000/sse 2>&1 | tee curl-sse.log
- python -c "import requests; r=requests.get('http://localhost:3000/sse', stream=True);
  for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=16):
    import time; print(len(chunk)); time.sleep(0.1)"
- node fetch + readable stream consumer to reproduce client backpressure:
  const res = await fetch(url); const reader = res.body.getReader(); while(true){ const {done, value} = await reader.read(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, 50)); console.log(value?.length); if(done) break; }

Server-side snippet (what we run):
- express SSE handler:
  res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream'); res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache'); res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive');
  // writing JSON as data events:
  res.write(`data: ${JSON.stringify({chunk: seq, payload})}

`); // call res.flush() when available

Hypotheses so far:
- Proxy buffering (nginx, alb) is coalescing small chunk writes when client is slow, creating long pauses. Need proxy_buffering off and chunked flush headers.
- Node's http2 / keepalive settings might batch small writes. res.flushHeaders() / res.flush() or using writable._writev behavior could help.
- Runtime's response encoder may be combining frames for perf; when client read is slow, TCP window/backpressure interacts with our batching logic, causing head-of-line blocking.
- If chunk boundary coincides with partial JSON token, client-side parser fails. We need framing that is resilient to partial reads (e.g., newline-delimited JSON with robust reassembly).

What I tried (and results):
- res.flush() after each write (using compression/gzip disabled) => improved in local but not through nginx.
- Added explicit "X-Accel-Buffering: no" and set proxy_buffering off in nginx => fixed buffering in many cases, still occasional stall via ALB.
- Switched to sending small keepalive comments (":

") every 10s to keep connection alive => reduced timeouts but didn't solve chunking order issues.
- Increased chunk size to send complete JSON objects in single write (serialize whole object, then single res.write) => reduced partial-JSON parse errors but increased latency for first tokens.

Logs / snippets (from curl -v):
* Connected to localhost (127.0.0.1) port 3000 (#0)
> GET /sse HTTP/1.1
> Host: localhost:3000
> User-Agent: curl/7.88.1
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< date: Tue, 05 Nov 2024 02:15:23 GMT

< 1e
{\"chunk\":1,\"payload\":\"...\"}

< 0a
{\"chunk\":2,\"payload\":\"...\"}

(then long pause)
< 0
* Connection #0 to host localhost left intact

Reproducer TODOs (next steps to make a small public repro):
- Create a minimal Node server that writes small JSON SSEs at 100ms intervals; include flags to toggle: useFlush=true, singleWrite=true, sendKeepalive=true.
- Add nginx config snippet with proxy_buffering on/off and run with docker-compose to reproduce cross-proxy differences.
- Add ALB-like proxy (envoy) to see if behavior matches customer reports.
- Instrument kernel/TCP cwnd? Maybe capture tcpdump to observe actual segmentization.

Potential quick fixes (short-term):
- Always send complete JSON objects in one res.write and avoid splitting tokens across writes.
- Add lightweight framing (prefix each message with length header) so client can reassemble even with partial reads.
- Disable proxy buffering where possible; surface config guidance for customers (nginx proxy_buffering off, X-Accel-Buffering: no).
- Add client examples that use incremental parser (ndjson or SSE event parsing) rather than JSON.parse on arbitrary chunks.

Notes for docs / runbook:
- This doc -> draft runbook entry describing when to set proxy_buffering off, when to prefer ndjson over raw JSON, and example server options (res.flush, compression off).
- Link to internal tickets: INF-789 (customer reported stalled SSE), PR 422 (attempted flush change).

Misc thoughts:
- Might be worth adding a middleware that ensures each res.write contains a complete framed message (serialize + prefix) to make runtime more robust by default.
- Investigate HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 differences: HTTP/2 uses frames and may avoid chunking issues but has its own flow control. Need tests.

Contact folks: Samir (kernel/tcp), Noah (nginx/proxy), Devon (client SDKs)

End of notes. Will flesh into reproducible repo once I confirm ALB behavior in staging.
summary: Personal debugging scratchpad for SSE/chunking/backpressure repro commands, logs, hypotheses and next steps
